chunks: Al-Rayyan b. al-Salt said: al-Rida (peace be upon him) recited a poem of Abd al-Mutalib to me:

All the people blame time, but there is nothing as blameworthy in our time as us. We blame our time when the fault is in us; if time could speak, it would have attacked us. Surely, a wolf leaves the flesh of a wolf, but we knowingly eat one another.

key_terms.ذئب: Wolf -- used as a contrast to show that even predators show more restraint than humans
key_terms.زمان: Time/era -- here used as a scapegoat for human failings
key_terms.عيب: Fault/blame -- the moral deficiency people project onto their circumstances

ai.seo_question: What poem did Imam al-Rida recite about blaming time for human failings?
ai.summary: This poem, attributed to Abd al-Mutalib (the Prophet's grandfather), was recited by Imam al-Rida (AS) to al-Rayyan b. al-Salt. It delivers a powerful ethical message about personal accountability: people blame their circumstances rather than acknowledging their own moral failings. The comparison with wolves -- that even wolves spare their own kind while humans devour each other -- serves as a sharp social critique of hypocrisy and mutual harm within the community.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Rayyan b. al-Salt said: al-Rida (as) recited a poem of `Abd al-Mutalib to me:

“All the people blame time, But there is nothing as blameworthy in our time as us, We blame our time when we are to blame, If time could talk, it would have attacked us. Surely, a wolf leaves the flesh of a wolf, But we knowingly eat [the flesh of] one another.”
